title: How a car engine works
examples: What is the difference between a petrol engine and a diesel engine?
Can you explain what happens to the exhaust gas?
How does the spark plug create the explosion?

explain.say: Today we are learning how a car engine makes power.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a piston engine. Look at the spark plug, the intake valve and the exhaust valve. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The engine uses four main movements called strokes.

items: Intake: Piston draws in fuel and air
Power: Spark ignites, pushing the piston down
Exhaust: Piston pushes out burnt gases

draw.text: Four Strokes: Intake, Compression, Power, Exhaust

explain.say: First, the intake stroke draws the fuel and air mixture in.
Next, the compression stroke squeezes this mixture tightly.
The power stroke happens when the spark plug ignites the mix.
Finally, the exhaust stroke pushes the burnt gases out of the engine.

faq.q: What is the main difference between the four strokes?
faq.a: The four strokes describe the cycle of air, fuel, and gas movement. The strokes are intake, compression, power, and exhaust.
asks: Can you name the four movements?
What does the engine cycle involve?

faq.q: Why is the compression stroke important?
faq.a: Compression is important because squeezing the mixture makes the explosion much more powerful. It increases the pressure greatly.
asks: Why do we squeeze the air?
What happens if we don't compress the fuel?

faq.q: How does an electric motor compare to this engine?
faq.a: An electric motor uses electricity to create motion directly. An engine uses controlled explosions to create motion.
asks: What is the energy source for each?

faq.q: Where do the exhaust gases go after the engine?
faq.a: The exhaust gases travel out through the exhaust system. This system usually leads to the tailpipe.
asks: What is the end of the exhaust?

faq.q: What is the role of the spark plug?
faq.a: The spark plug provides the electrical spark needed to ignite the fuel and air mixture. This starts the power stroke.
asks: Does the spark plug make the fire?

facts: The four strokes are intake, compression, power, and exhaust.
In the power stroke, controlled combustion pushes the piston down.
Electric motors use electromagnetic force to create rotational motion.
The piston moves up and down inside the cylinder.

quiz.say: Which stroke involves drawing the fuel and air mixture into the cylinder?
quiz.why: The intake stroke is specifically designed to draw the necessary mixture into the cylinder.

wrong.1: Compression happens after the mixture is already inside the cylinder.
wrong.2: Power is the result of the explosion, not the drawing in of air.
wrong.3: Exhaust is for pushing out the burnt gases, not bringing in fresh air.

quiz.say: If an engine is running, what is the primary source of force during the power stroke?
quiz.why: The power stroke is directly caused by the rapid expansion from burning fuel and air.

wrong.1: Spring tension is not the main force driving the piston in this cycle.
wrong.2: Electric current is used to start the process, but combustion provides the main force.
wrong.3: While air pressure is involved, the controlled burning of fuel adds the necessary force.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly compares an engine to an electric motor?

options.show: Engine uses combustion, motor uses electricity.
options.say: Engine uses combustion, motor uses electricity.

quiz.why: The key difference is the energy source: chemical energy in the engine versus electrical energy in the motor.

wrong.0: Only internal combustion engines require a spark plug for ignition.
wrong.1: While pistons move linearly, electric motors are better known for creating rotational motion.
wrong.3: Electric motors typically use magnets and coils, not pistons and cylinders.
